title: Pulsed Field Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias: A Systematic Review and Dual-Framework (Frequentist and Bayesian) Meta-Analysis.
summary: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is being applied to ventricular arrhythmias, but human evidence remains limited to small, single-arm studies. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov, major conference archives, and reference lists through March 1, 2026, for human studies of catheter-based PFA for ventricular tachycardia (VT) or premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) enrolling at least 5 patients. We pooled study-defined acute procedural success with two complementary analyses of the same data: a frequentist random-effects model and a Bayesian binomial-logit hierarchical model that expresses the same evidence as posterior probabilities. Seven unique studies (274 patients enrolled; 12 study arms, 270 arm-level patients) were included. Pooled acute success was 84.3% (95% confidence interval 77.7-89.2%) across 6 VT arms (n = 173) and 86.6% (80.6-91.0%) across 6 PVC arms (n = 97); the posterior probability that the pooled parameter success exceeds 80% was 97.1% for VT and 96.7% for PVCs. Major complications occurred in 5.8% (3.5-9.4%; 7 studies). Coronary spasm was the principal PFA-specific event; no study performed late angiography or intravascular imaging, and phrenic nerve and esophageal outcomes were largely not assessed. One study measured hemolysis systematically. Recurrence during available follow-up (3.3-9.6 months per study) was 36% for VT across 5 arms and 22% for PVCs. These findings support acute procedural feasibility. Durability, safety, and comparative effectiveness remain uncertain and require standardized prospective assessment.

title: Time From Cardioversion to First Catheter Ablation and the Risk of Recurrence of Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Direct current cardioversion (DCCV) offers symptomatic relief from persistent atrial fibrillation (persAF), and potentially reverses atrial remodeling, but arrhythmia recurrence frequently follows. This study explores the association between the cardioversion-to-ablation-time (CAT) and long-term recurrence of persAF in a real-world cohort of patients undergoing ablation.

METHODS: A total of 1197 patients with persAF at a large multicenter healthcare system who received DCCV before their first catheter ablation were followed to the endpoint of freedom from persAF recurrence.

RESULTS: Patients (66 ± 9 years old, 73% men, CHA2DS2VASc 2.3 ± 1.3, moderate or severe left atrial dilation 44%) had a mean of 1.9 ± 1.5 DCCV prior to the first catheter ablation with 53% taking an antiarrhythmic drug (AAD) at the time of catheter ablation. Cryoablation, radiofrequency ablation or a combination was used for primary pulmonary vein isolation with 30% of patients receiving additional lesion sets for posterior wall isolation and/or cavotricuspid isthmus or mitral annular isthmus block. Over a median follow-up of 506 (IQR 81-1112) days, recurrence of persAF after catheter ablation was highly associated with longer CAT time (adjusted HR = 1.20 per tertile increase in CAT; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Patients with shorter CAT are more likely to be free from persAF after first catheter ablation. If confirmed in a prospective setting, this finding may have important clinical implications.

title: Sex-Based Differences in Outcomes of Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in Patients With Left Bundle Branch Block: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) improves outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and left bundle branch block (LBBB), and several studies suggest that women respond better than men. However, most evidence comes from populations that mix LBBB with other conduction disturbances. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of sex-specific CRT outcomes restricted to patients with LBBB. PubMed, Scopus, and Excerpta Medica database (Embase) were searched from inception to November 2024 in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Twelve studies (4,072 patients; 1,564 women) were included. Studies of conventional biventricular pacing (BVP) formed the primary analysis, and left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) arms were added in sensitivity analyses. Random-effects models were used. In the primary analysis, women had a greater improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) than men (mean difference (MD) 2.83%, 95% CI 0.16-5.51; I²=81%), with a larger difference in studies published after 2010 (MD 4.07%, 95% CI 0.42-7.72). Women also had lower all-cause mortality (RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.94; I²=0%) and fewer heart failure hospitalizations (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.54-0.99), although the latter estimate was based on only two studies. Post-CRT QRS duration did not differ by sex. Adding the single available LBBAP arm gave a similar LVEF estimate (MD 2.67%, 95% CI 0.43-4.90). However, the LVEF difference lost statistical significance when any of four of the six BVP studies were omitted; its 95% prediction interval crossed zero (-6.04% to 11.71%), and the mortality estimate depended largely on one large study. Among patients with LBBB undergoing CRT, female sex was associated with more favorable outcomes. Because women more often had non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, less often had atrial fibrillation, and had smaller ventricles, these findings reflect an association rather than an independent effect of sex.

title: Vaccination, inflammation, and atrial fibrillation: expanding the boundaries of cardiovascular prevention.
Weekly Journal Scan: The anticoagulation dilemma in intermediate-risk atrial fibrillation.
Late gadolinium enhancement and recovery of left ventricular function after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation.
summary:
AIMS: Improvement in left ventricular (LV) function after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation is heterogeneous. Ventricular late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) may limit reverse remodelling, but the relative importance of LGE pattern and burden remain uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicentre study, patients with AF and LV systolic dysfunction undergoing catheter ablation were evaluated. LV response was defined as ≥10% absolute improvement in LV ejection fraction or improvement to ≥50% on follow-up echocardiography. Quantitative LGE burden, LGE pattern, and clinical variables were assessed to identify predictors of LV response following AF ablation. Among 134 patients [mean age 62.8 ± 11.7 years; 84.3% male; median follow-up 22.2 months (IQR 13.1-45.6)], 101 (75.4%) demonstrated LV response. LV non-responders were more likely to have ventricular LGE (69.7% vs. 46.5%, P = 0.02) and had greater LGE burden (6.6 ± 4.9% vs. 3.3 ± 3.2%, P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing LGE burden was independently associated with a reduced likelihood of LV response (RR 0.96 per 1% increase, 95% CI 0.92-0.99; P = 0.036), alongside longer QRS duration (RR 0.99 per ms, 95% CI 0.98-0.99; P = 0.01) whereas an unknown heart failure aetiology was associated with an increased likelihood of LV response (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.06-1.76; P = 0.01). No specific LGE pattern predicted LV response. Mediation analysis demonstrated a minimal indirect effect through rhythm status (∼2%).

CONCLUSION: In patients with AF and LV systolic dysfunction undergoing catheter ablation, the extent of ventricular fibrosis, rather than its visual distribution, is associated with the likelihood of LV response. Quantitative LGE burden may help identify patients with myocardial remodelling reserve post-catheter ablation.

title: Preoperative depression or anxiety and late new-onset atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery: an observational cohort study.
summary:
AIMS: The aim was to study the association between preoperative depression or anxiety and incidence of late new-onset atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Data from five national registers including 44 338 patients who underwent primary cardiac surgery in Sweden between 2006 and 2020 were used, excluding those with a prior diagnosis of atrial fibrillation. Follow-up for atrial fibrillation occurred >30 days after surgery. Cox regression models were used to estimate the association between preoperative depression or anxiety and new late-onset atrial fibrillation in the total study population and according to sex and age categories. In total, 1037 (12%) of the patients with preoperative depression or anxiety, and 5036 (14%) of those without, developed late new-onset atrial fibrillation following cardiac surgery. Patients with depression or anxiety had an increased risk of developing atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.09; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.01-1.17]. Sex-specific analysis showed that men with depression or anxiety had an increased risk of late new-onset atrial fibrillation (aHR 1.14; 95% CI 1.05-1.25), whereas this increased risk was not observed in women (aHR 1.00; 95% CI 0.89-1.13).

CONCLUSION: Patients with preoperative depression or anxiety undergoing primary cardiac surgery had an increased risk of late new-onset atrial fibrillation. This association was predominantly observed in men under 75 years of age. Routine screening for depression and anxiety can identify patients at risk. Comprehensive care, including mental health support, lifestyle changes, and medication management, may reduce the risk of late new-onset atrial fibrillation.

title: Safety and efficacy of irrigated-tip catheter ablation guided by three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping for atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia: the WATER ATTAC study.
Evaluation of physician alerts to improve treatment for prevention of stroke in atrial fibrillation patients.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulants reduce stroke risk in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients, yet a 25%-35% treatment gap exists for high-risk individuals. To address this, an automated electronic health record alert was implemented for untreated AF patients meeting guideline criteria (CHA2DS2VASc score ≥2 for males, ≥3 for females) with no prior history of anticoagulant purchase.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the efficacy of the clinical decision support alert in promoting anticoagulant prescribing-specifically direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs)-to align treatment with international standards.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed demographic, socioeconomic, and prescription dispensing data. Alert effectiveness was defined as the percentage of patients who successfully purchased anticoagulants following a physician-received alert during a clinical visit.

RESULTS: The alert triggered for 2,412 patients (mean age 74.6 ± 9.0 years; 41.5% female). Only 0.43% of alerts were actively declined by physicians for medical reasons, confirming high clinical appropriateness. Overall, 26.53% (n = 640) of targeted patients subsequently purchased DOACs. However, equitable gaps remained, as Arabs and females were significantly less likely to receive prescriptions.

CONCLUSION: An automated alert reached AF patients whom guideline recommendations alone had not, and narrowed but did not close the anticoagulant treatment gap. The remaining gap lies mainly in the consultation rather than in patient identification, and is wider among women and in the Arab sector.

title: The Index of Cardio-Electrophysiological Balance Is Associated with Malignant Ventricular Arrhythmia and New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in STEMI Patients.
summary: Introduction: The index of cardio-electrophysiological balance (iCEB) has been associated with various cardiac arrhythmias. However, the relationship between iCEB and ventricular arrhythmias (VA) as well as atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the association between iCEB and the development of malignant VA and new-onset AF in patients with STEMI. Method: A total of 250 patients presenting with STEMI (49 females, 201 males; mean age 59.3 ± 12.5 years) were included in this retrospective observational cohort study. A standard 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) was obtained from all patients at the time of hospital admission. In addition to routine ECG parameters, iCEB (QT/QRS) was calculated from the recorded ECGs. Patients were monitored for the occurrence of malignant VA (sustained ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation) and new-onset AF within the first 48 h. The study population was divided into groups based on the presence or absence of malignant VA and new-onset AF, and all parameters were compared between these groups. Results: QT interval, QTc interval, JT interval, iCEB, and iCEBc values were found to be significantly higher in patients with malignant VA compared to those without malignant VA. Similarly, QT interval, QTc interval, JT interval, iCEB, and iCEBc values were significantly elevated in patients with new-onset AF compared to those without new-onset AF. In logistic regression analysis, iCEB and JT interval were identified as independent predictors of malignant VA (OR = 1.051, 95% CI: 1.015-1.132, p = 0.016 and OR = 1.013, 95% CI: 1.003-1.025, p = 0.013, respectively). Likewise, iCEB and JT interval were also independent predictors of new-onset AF (OR = 1.099, 95% CI: 1.033-1.169, p = 0.003 and OR = 1.018, 95% CI: 1.006-1.030, p = 0.002, respectively). Discussion: In our study, iCEB measured at the time of admission in patients with STEMI was shown to be a significant adjunctive parameter in identifying both malignant VA and new-onset AF. Therefore, STEMI patients with elevated iCEB values should be closely monitored for the development of arrhythmias.

title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Nomogram to Predict Actionable Arrhythmias During Implantable Cardiac Monitoring in Patients with Unexplained Syncope.
summary: Prediction tools for actionable arrhythmias after implantable cardiac monitor (ICM) implantation in patients with unexplained syncope remain limited. This dual-center retrospective study included 302 patients divided chronologically into development (n = 91) and temporal validation (n = 211) cohorts. The endpoint was the first ICM-detected arrhythmia prompting permanent pacemaker or defibrillator implantation, catheter ablation, initiation of Vaughan Williams Class I or III antiarrhythmic drugs, or oral anticoagulation. A multivariable Cox model was developed and internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples, repeating variable selection and model fitting. During a median follow-up of 23.4 months, 78 patients reached the endpoint, including 32 in the development cohort and 46 in the temporal validation cohort. The nomogram included age, a history of recurrent syncope, and first-degree atrioventricular block. The optimism-corrected C-index was 0.720 in development. In temporal validation, the C-index was 0.707 (95% confidence interval, 0.623-0.790), and the 12- and 24-month time-dependent areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.733 and 0.741, respectively. The nomogram showed moderate discrimination in temporal validation at the same two centers. The model underestimated risk at 12 months, whereas mean predicted risk was closer to observed risk at 24 months.

title: Differential Recurrence Risk in Paroxysmal Versus Persistent Atrial Fibrillation Post-Catheter Ablation: HFpEF as an Independent Predictor.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) have bidirectional pathophysiological interactions. Although HFpEF has been associated with arrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA), whether its impact differs across AF subtypes remains incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the prognostic impact of HFpEF on AF recurrence following RFCA in paroxysmal versus persistent AF.

METHODS: A total of 509 patients who underwent RFCA for AF were enrolled in our retrospective study. These patients were categorized into two groups: the normal group and the HFpEF group. The primary endpoint was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias (≥30 s) after the initial 3-month blanking period post-index ablation, without any antiarrhythmic drugs.

RESULTS: HFpEF was present in 15.9% of the cohort. At the 12-month follow-up visit, sinus rhythm maintenance was recorded in 62.7% of the patients in the HFpEF group versus 82.0% in the normal group (p < 0.001). A multivariable analysis identified HFpEF as an independent predictor of AF recurrence (hazard ratio [HR]: 2.06, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.26-3.38, p = 0.004). After 1:1 propensity score matching, HFpEF remained an independent predictor of AF recurrence (HR 1.93, 95% CI: 1.06-3.50, p = 0.03). A subgroup analysis showed a robust association in paroxysmal AF (HR = 6.00, 95% CI: 3.07-11.73, p < 0.001) but not in persistent AF (HR = 1.43, 95%CI: 0.80-2.55, p = 0.231), with a significant interaction (p for interaction = 0.022). During the 12-month follow-up visit, an improvement in the New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification could be seen in 82.7% of the cohort, with all Class III patients showing a functional improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: There is an increased risk of recurrence in patients with HFpEF post-ablation, particularly among patients with paroxysmal AF. Notably, catheter ablation remains effective at improving the NYHA functional class, even in HFpEF patients. These findings support the utilization of HFpEF as a key indicator for pre-procedural risk stratification.

title: A Random Survival Forest Model Incorporating Dual Left Atrial Diameters for Predicting Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Left Unilateral Thoracoscopic Ablation.
summary: Background: Left atrial anteroposterior diameter (LAAP) is commonly used to assess left atrial remodeling and recurrence risk after thoracoscopic atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, but may incompletely reflect atrial enlargement, whereas volumetric assessment has equipment- and operator-related limitations. Our study aimed to develop a prediction approach for AF recurrence by incorporating complementary left atrial diameters. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 563 patients undergoing left unilateral thoracoscopic ablation, with 430 patients from January 2018 to December 2022 assigned to the training set and 133 patients from January 2023 to December 2024 assigned to the testing set. Model development was performed in the training cohort. Model performance was evaluated using Harrell's C-index and receiver operating characteristic curves. The model was further converted into a risk score system (LATA) for clinical application. Results: LAAP and left atrial superoinferior diameter (LASI) were significant predictors of 1-year AF recurrence, with cutoffs of 4.7 cm and 7.0 cm, respectively. An RSF model incorporating six selected variables, including LAAP and LASI, achieved AUCs of 0.834 in training set and 0.795 in testing set. The LATA score showed good discrimination and effectively stratified recurrence risk. Conclusions: Our machine learning model and score system (LATA) combining LAAP and LASI showed favorable predictive performance and potential clinical utility.

title: Incessant Fascicular Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation After MitraClip Procedure: A Case Report.
summary: We report a case of a 52-year-old man with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and advanced renal failure, who presented with electrical storm 4 months after concomitant MitraClip and TriClip procedure for severe functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. Electrocardiography showed VT with right bundle branch block morphology and superior axis. The VT was refractory to antiarrhythmic drugs and cardioversion despite sedation and hemodynamic support. An emergent electrophysiological study was consistent with fascicular reentry originating from the left posterior fascicle, arising on a background of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular scar. Catheter ablation targeting the left posterior fascicle rendered the VT non-inducible. During one year of device-monitored follow-up, no recurrent ventricular tachycardia (VT) was documented.

title: Conduction Across the Donor-Recipient Anastomosis as a Substrate for Atrial Arrhythmia After Heart Transplantation.
summary: Late atrial arrhythmia after heart transplantation is usually attributed to rejection, and the donor-recipient anastomosis is assumed to isolate the native pulmonary venous cuff. We mapped it in three recipients treated with pulsed field ablation. In the first, native posterior wall electrograms cycled at half the tachycardia cycle length and conducted intermittently to the donor atrium until anastomotic ablation isolated them. The second had septal reentry despite a durable anastomosis; the third had reconnection of previously isolated pulmonary veins. Rejection was excluded in all. Although limited to three patients, these findings support mapping the anastomosis before attributing arrhythmia to rejection.

title: Leadless Pacemaker AVEIR VR: Performance of the Rate-Responsive Sensor During Exercise.
summary:
BACKGROUND: To date, no published data have evaluated the exercise performance of the AVEIR VR leadless pacemaker.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess, during bicycle ergometer exercise testing, the relationship between the intrinsic sinus heart rate and the ventricular rate delivered by the AVEIR VR pacemaker. Patients with atrial fibrillation or those unable to perform exercise testing were excluded.

METHODS: Patients underwent a bicycle ergometer exercise test using a workload protocol normalized to body weight (W/kg) according to their level of physical activity (sedentary or active). Simultaneous device interrogation was performed throughout the test. Intrinsic sinus heart rate and paced heart rate (or the projected paced heart rate in non-pacemaker-dependent patients) were recorded. Sensor latency was defined as the time required to achieve a 10-beats/min increase in paced heart rate above baseline.

RESULTS: Between January and October 2025, 13 patients were included (69.9 ± 12.7 years; 23% women). Five patients were physically active, and eight patients were pacemaker-dependent. The mean sensor latency was 3.5 min in pacemaker-dependent patients and 2.7 min in non-pacemaker-dependent patients. Rate-response gain required adjustment in 38.5% of patients following exercise testing. Base rate and/or the maximum heart rate response were modified in 76.9% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Exercise testing in patients implanted with an AVEIR VR leadless pacemaker demonstrated an overall appropriate rate-response, although with a non-negligible sensor latency. A substantial proportion of patients required post-exercise optimization of rate-response programming, highlighting the value of exercise-guided device programming to improve physiological chronotropic adaptation.

title: Catheter Ablation Outcomes in Patients With Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation and Resolved Atrial Thrombus.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation therapy can achieve thrombus resolution in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), ablation outcomes in this population remain poorly defined. We compared ablation outcomes between patients with NVAF and resolved atrial thrombus and those without a thrombus history.

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled consecutive NVAF patients undergoing initial catheter ablation. Group A (patients with documented atrial thrombus that had resolved prior to ablation) was enrolled between August 2019 and December 2022; Group B (patients without a history of atrial thrombus) was enrolled between July 2022 and December 2022. The primary endpoint was atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence within 12 months, defined as any atrial tachyarrhythmia lasting ≥30 s beyond the 3-month blanking period.

RESULTS: In total, 21 patients in Group A and 291 patients in Group B were analyzed. Compared to patients in Group B, patients in Group A were younger (60.0 [57.0-66.0] years vs. 67.0 [60.0-71.0] years, p = 0.011) and exhibited higher prevalence of non-paroxysmal AF (81.0% vs. 52.6%, p = 0.012), heart failure (28.6% vs. 6.5%, p = 0.001), vascular disease (28.6% vs. 5.5%, p < 0.001), and elevated B-type natriuretic peptide levels (95.2% vs. 59.8%, p = 0.001). Group A demonstrated significantly higher atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence (HR 2.41, 95% CI 1.27-4.55; p = 0.007) and had a higher prevalence of low-voltage areas (LVAs) (66.7% vs 35.1%, p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Patients with NVAF and resolved atrial thrombus had a significantly higher atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation, likely reflecting more advanced atrial substrate remodeling, as indicated by the higher prevalence of LVAs.

title: Right ventricular ejection time and mortality in acute heart failure with atrial fibrillation in older adults.
summary: Right ventricular ejection time is visible on routine pulsed-wave Doppler recordings, but its relation to outcome in acute heart failure with atrial fibrillation is uncertain. We examined 320 consecutive adults hospitalized at one center from 2014 through 2018. Echocardiography was performed from 27 days before to 29 days after admission, and mortality analyses used delayed-entry Cox models. Right ventricular ejection time was available in 247 patients; the primary complete-case cohort comprised 240 patients with 98 deaths. Each 1-standard-deviation (38.0-ms) longer ejection time was associated with a lower adjusted hazard of all-cause death (hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% confidence interval, 0.59-0.89; p = 0.002). The estimate was similar after additional adjustment for left ventricular and left atrial strain (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval, 0.60-0.92; p = 0.006). Evidence of time dependence was borderline, suggesting a stronger association during the first year with attenuation thereafter. Ejection time was not clearly associated with subsequent first heart failure rehospitalization. Among patients alive at the time of measurement, shorter right ventricular ejection time was associated with higher mortality in this exploratory cohort; this routine Doppler interval is a potentially informative prognostic correlate.

title: AI-Based Multi-Year Prediction of Incident Dementia in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation
summary: The burden of dementia is rising rapidly, but preventive strategies remain limited and few tools exist to identify individuals at risk a priori. This unmet need is especially relevant in atrial fibrillation (AF), a rapidly growing population at increased risk of dementia. We present MIND-AF, an AI-based model to predict 3 to 5-year risk of dementia from readily available bedside data. Developed in 108,672 AF patients without prior dementia within an academic-community network in California, MIND-AF predicted incident dementia in a held-out test cohort (n=32,238) with a C-index of 0.82 over 3.8 +/- 4.6 years after AF diagnosis, outperforming age and clinical risk scores (CHA2DS2-VASc, HATCH; all p < 0.001). MIND-AF enabled a priori stratification into low, medium and high-risk groups, with dementia incidence of 0.34%, 1.59% and 6.3% over 3 years and 0.7%, 3.4% and 13.0% over 5 years from AF diagnosis, respectively. MIND-AF provided similar performance in a sealed external population of 58,826 demographically distinct patients in Georgia (C-index 0.80), as well as pre-specified cohorts without neurodegenerative disease, mild cognitive impairment, stroke or transient ischemic attack. MIND-AF, freely available as an online web application, provides scalable point-of-care risk stratification for incident dementia in patients diagnosed with AF, is robust to baseline neurocognitive and cerebrovascular baseline states, and provides a bedside framework for intensified dementia prevention.

title: Trends in Atrial Fibrillation and Atrial Flutter Management in Reproductive-Age Women: GWTG-AFib Registry.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The occurrence of cardiac arrhythmias in reproductive-aged women has increased in the United States. Management remains challenging due to limited guideline evidence and the maternal/fetal risks associated with many anti-arrhythmia therapies.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize prescription patterns and management trends in the treatment of atrial arrhythmias in reproductive-aged women over the past decade.

METHODS: The Get With The Guidelines (GWTG)-Atrial Fibrillation registry was queried between 2013 and 2024, and all women of reproductive-age (≤50 years) hospitalized with atrial fibrillation (AFib) or flutter (AFL) were included. Medications were classified into low risk, conflicted, and avoided/contraindicated during pregnancy. Discharge prescribing patterns of the most used anticoagulants, antiarrhythmic agents, and rate control medications were analyzed. Temporal trends were assessed using the Cochrane-Armitage test, and group comparisons were performed using Chi-square analysis.

RESULTS: Among 3,755 hospitalizations for AFib or AFL in reproductive-aged women between 2013 and 2024, 2,732 (72.8%) were discharged on an anticoagulant, while 1,380 (36.8%) received an antiarrhythmic medication. Overall, 75.3% of encounters were discharged on medications generally classified as avoided/contraindicated during pregnancy, with a significant upward trend in the use of such medications over the study period (p<0.05), largely driven by increased anticoagulant use. New-onset AFib accounted for 651 hospitalizations (20.5%), with rhythm-control strategies used more frequently than rate control in this subgroup (62%).

CONCLUSION: The frequent and increasing use of medications with potential pregnancy-related concerns highlights the need for reproductive-specific guidance that integrates arrhythmia management with reproductive planning and medication safety.

title: Comparison of Pulsed Field Ablation Technologies for Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: a Systematic Review and Pairwise Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Commercial pulsed field ablation (PFA) platforms differ in catheter geometry, mapping integration, irrigation, and energy-delivery strategy.

OBJECTIVE: To compare FARAPULSE, VARIPULSE, PulseSelect, Affera/Sphere-9, and Volt across procedural, biological, safety, and efficacy outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched through October 8, 2026. Separate random-effects pairwise meta-analyses were performed for each direct device comparison. Exploratory analyses examined lesion strategy, publication year, electroanatomic mapping, and intracardiac echocardiography.

RESULTS: Forty-six observational reports representing 43 studies were included. VARIPULSE workflows used less fluoroscopy than FARAPULSE (MD -13.54 minutes; 95% CI -18.89 to -8.19) and PulseSelect (MD -11.45; 95% CI -16.96 to -5.94), while Affera/Sphere-9 used less than FARAPULSE (MD -7.20; 95% CI -10.27 to -4.14). Affera/Sphere-9 showed less haptoglobin depletion than FARAPULSE, PulseSelect, and VARIPULSE; Volt showed less than FARAPULSE. No platform consistently shortened procedure time or differed clearly in overall complications or acute kidney injury. Comparative durability remained limited outside FARAPULSE and PulseSelect.

CONCLUSION: The platforms showed distinct workflow and biomarker profiles without one uniformly superior system. VARIPULSE and Affera/Sphere-9 workflows used less fluoroscopy in available direct comparisons, and Affera/Sphere-9 and Volt showed less haptoglobin depletion in selected comparisons. These biomarker findings did not establish a renal or hard clinical advantage. Comparative durability remains uncertain.

title: Safety and efficacy of pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation in elderly patients.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Data regarding the safety and clinical efficacy of pulsed field ablation (PFA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) in older patients are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and impact on healthcare utilization of PFA for AF in patients aged ≥75 years.

METHODS: This sub-study of the multicenter SENTINEL registry included consecutive patients undergoing first-time AF ablation with a pentaspline PFA system across 13 centers in Australia and New Zealand. Outcomes were compared among patients aged <65 years, 65-74 years, and ≥75 years. Primary endpoints were major procedural complications and healthcare utilization (composite of unplanned rehospitalization for atrial arrhythmia, cardioversion and repeat catheter ablation).

RESULTS: Of 1,611 patients, 769 (48%) were aged <65 years, 573 (36%) aged 65-74 years and 269 (17%) aged ≥75 years. Patients aged ≥75 years had greater comorbidity burden, and higher prevalence of non-paroxysmal AF and left atrial dilatation. Major procedural complications were uncommon and similar across age groups (0.9%, 0.2% and 0.7%, respectively; p=0.48). Over a median follow-up of 426 days, healthcare utilization (10.8%, 12.0% and 10.0%; p=0.61) and arrhythmia recurrence (17.2%, 19.5% and 19.3%; p=0.39) were comparable across age groups. Age ≥75 years was not independently associated with healthcare utilization or arrhythmia recurrence after multivariable adjustment and propensity score matching.

CONCLUSION: In this large multicenter study, low procedural complication rates and comparable clinical outcomes were observed across age groups following PFA for AF, supporting individualized selection of patients for AF ablation rather than categorical exclusion based on age alone.

title: PVI Using the Fixed Loop PFA in Paroxysmal AF: One-Year Outcomes with Continuous Implantable Loop Recorder Monitoring.
summary:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is a promising non-thermal energy modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF), with favorable safety and efficacy data. However, published data rely on intermittent rhythm monitoring, which likely underestimates recurrence rates. We sought to evaluate 12-month outcomes of PVI using the PulseSelect™ system in patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF) monitored continuously with implantable loop recorders (ILRs), and to characterize the performance of a standardized "6-4" lesion delivery workflow.

METHODS: This is a single-center, prospective observational study of consecutive patients aged <75 years with symptomatic, PAF and an ILR. All ablations were performed using the PulseSelect™ catheter using a standardized workflow delivering 6 antral and 4 ostial PFA applications per pulmonary vein (PV), guided by left-sided intracardiac echocardiography. The primary endpoint was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias from 91 to 365 days post-ablation, assessed by continuous ILR.

RESULTS: Twenty-five patients (13 male, 12 females; mean age 68.3 ± 4.2 years; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.5 ± 0.6) underwent PVI between August and November 2024. Acute PVI was achieved in 100% of PVs. Median procedure and left atrial dwell times were 74 (IQR 48-82) and 44 (IQR 34-57) minutes, respectively. Mean fluoroscopy time was 3.2 ± 1.7 minutes. At 12 months, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias off class I/III antiarrhythmic drugs was observed in 22 of 25 patients (88%).

CONCLUSIONS: In a PAF cohort with mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring, the PulseSelect™ system using a standardized workflow achieved universal acute PVI and favorable 12-month arrhythmia-free outcomes with an excellent safety profile. Continuous monitoring provides the most rigorous assessment of freedom from recurrence.

title: Long-term air pollution and COVID-19 severity in New York City hospitalized patients: Mediation by pre-existing atrial fibrillation and myocardial infarction.
summary: Evidence links long-term air pollution to COVID-19 severity. Given ongoing COVID-19 hospitalizations, we explored how historical pollution influences COVID-19 outcomes. We examined whether pre-existing cardiovascular conditions, both major predictors of severe COVID-19 and strongly associated with pollution, mediate the relationship between historical pollution and adverse COVID-19 outcomes. We studied NYC residents hospitalized with COVID-19 (3/1/2020-2/28/2021; N = 20,118), using harmonized electronic health records. Historical exposure to particulate matter (PM2.5), black carbon (BC), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and ozone (O3) was assigned using 11-year annual averages (2009-2019) from NYC Community Air Survey ZIP Code data. Logistic regression estimated the odds of 15 cardiovascular conditions as mediators (e.g., myocardial infarction (MI), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure, hypertension). Modified Poisson regression estimated risks of adverse COVID-19 outcomes, including acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), pneumonia, ventilation, and dialysis, and Cox regression estimated hazards of fatality and discharge, adjusting for age, sex, smoking, environmental vulnerability, and exposure-mediator interaction. In the first wave (March-June 2020), historical PM2.5, BC, and NO2 increased risk of ARDS, pneumonia, and dialysis; inverse estimates found for O3. Pre-existing AF and MI accounted for the largest indirect effects of long-term PM2.5 exposure on ARDS, dialysis, ventilation, and fatality outcomes. Nearly 25% of the effect of long-term PM2.5 on ARDS, dialysis, and ventilation was mediated by AF or MI. Overall, historical pollution is linked to adverse COVID-19, with AF and MI as potential mediators. Findings encourage research on long-term pollution influencing pandemic outcomes and strategies to improve cardiovascular health in communities experiencing long-term pollution.

title: Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation: Detection, Risk Stratification, and Clinical Management.
summary: Subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF) presents a clinical challenge in which increasingly sensitive detection has outpaced the evidence needed to guide treatment. This review integrates recent evidence on detection, thromboembolic risk, disease progression, and clinical management, with particular emphasis on studies published since 2024 and their implications for Japanese practice. Implantable monitors, patch electrocardiography, consumer wearables, and home devices broaden opportunities for detecting asymptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF), while artificial intelligence may refine selection for monitoring. However, differences in diagnostic definitions, population risk, and AF burden complicate the translation of greater diagnostic yield into stroke prevention; pooled screening evidence suggests only modest benefit. Secondary analyses of ARTESiA and NOAH-AFNET 6 have challenged reliance on episode duration alone. Recent SCAF duration and frequency were not significantly associated with thromboembolic risk in ARTESiA, and atrial high-rate episode duration did not significantly modify treatment effects in NOAH-AFNET 6. These findings do not establish a safe duration threshold. Patient characteristics and progression to clinical AF or longer episodes remain relevant to longitudinal assessment, although subgroup treatment estimates require cautious interpretation. Randomized evidence indicates that direct oral anticoagulants reduce ischemic stroke but increase major bleeding, without a demonstrated mortality benefit. Management therefore requires confirmation of the arrhythmia, individualized assessment of benefit and harm, shared decision-making, comorbidity management, and continued surveillance. European, American, and Japanese recommendations differ in terminology, duration criteria, risk scores, and recommendation strength; the Japanese device-detected AF recommendation warrants reassessment in light of contemporary randomized evidence. Trials of screening, rhythm-guided anticoagulation, rhythm control, and factor XI inhibition address important remaining uncertainties, but results from clinical AF populations will require careful evaluation before application to SCAF.

title: Chronic Total Occlusions and Their Relationship With Ventricular Function and Arrhythmia.
summary: Chronic total occlusions (CTOs) are common and have an estimated prevalence of 20% in patients with coronary artery disease. Their presence has been associated with worse outcomes in both stable coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndromes, including a higher incidence of ventricular arrhythmias and impaired left ventricular function. A bidirectional relationship exists between left ventricular impairment and ventricular arrhythmias: left ventricular impairment increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias, and ventricular arrhythmias can further depress left ventricular function. Despite these relationships, there has been minimal evidence demonstrating a clear prognostic benefit of revascularization, and current guidelines recommend revascularization of CTOs primarily for refractory angina. This review aims to describe the relationship between CTOs, ventricular arrhythmias, and left ventricular function and evaluate the current evidence on whether revascularization can reduce ventricular arrhythmia risk or improve left ventricular function.

title: Purkinje Activation Trajectory for Ventricular Fibrillation Initiation in Three-Dimensional Image.
summary: Initiation of VF was associated with a gradual shift in trajectory of the Purkinje activation cluster and appeared to arise from reentry between the Purkinje fibers and ventricular myocardium.

title: Pronounced Mitral Annular Disjunction Is Associated with Increased Ventricular Arrhythmia Burden After Mitral Valve Surgery.
summary: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been associated with ventricular arrhythmias in mitral valve prolapse, while postoperative ventricular arrhythmia burden remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to assess objective ventricular arrhythmia burden after mitral valve surgery in patients with and without pronounced MAD (pMAD). In this retrospective single-center cohort with cross-sectional postoperative rhythm assessment, patients undergoing mitral valve surgery for Barlow's disease between 2014 and 2023 were stratified by intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography into pMAD (≥8 mm) and non-pMAD (<8 mm). All patients were invited to structured postoperative follow-up, including 24-h Holter monitoring at variable time points after surgery. Valid recordings were available in 126 of 246 patients (51.2%; 66 pMAD, 60 non-pMAD). Patients with pMAD had a significantly higher ventricular ectopic burden than those without pMAD (median 20.1 vs. 5.5 VES/h; p = 0.005). Non-sustained ventricular tachycardia was documented exclusively in the pMAD group (15.2% vs. 0%; p = 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, pMAD remained associated with high ventricular ectopic burden (OR 3.38, 95% CI 1.32-8.64; p = 0.011). These findings identify pMAD as a marker of increased postoperative ventricular arrhythmia burden after mitral valve surgery for Barlow's disease.

title: Comparative Analysis of Multielectrode Mapping Catheter Designs in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: High-density (HD) electroanatomical mapping is routinely used for scar-related ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. The performance of multielectrode mapping catheters with different array designs has not been directly compared.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the procedural performance of two different multielectrode mapping catheter designs-a flexible spline catheter (SC) and a fixed paddle catheter (PC) in scar-related VT ablation.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 104 consecutive patients who underwent left ventricular scar-related VT ablation (SC, n = 44; PC, n = 60). The primary endpoint was acute procedural success, defined as non-inducibility of the clinical VT after ablation. Secondary endpoints included procedural efficiency, VT inducibility, VT morphology burden, and procedural and in-hospital adverse events.

RESULTS: Acute procedural success was achieved in 95.5% of SC and 98.3% of PC procedures (p = 0.57). Procedure duration, LV mapping time, mapping point count, fluoroscopy time, and adverse-event rates were comparable between groups. Overall VT inducibility (mechanical or programmed induction) was similar (81.8% vs. 76.7%; p = 0.63); however, ≥3 distinct inducible VT morphologies were significantly more frequent with the spline catheter than with the paddle catheter (38.6% vs. 11.7%; p = 0.002). During follow-up, rates of VT recurrence (34.5% vs. 20.0%; p = 0.19) and repeat ablation (13.8% vs. 7.3%; p = 0.44) did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Both catheter designs achieved comparable acute procedural success, procedural efficiency, and safety in scar-related VT ablation. Procedures with the spline catheter were associated with a higher inducible VT morphology burden; this hypothesis-generating finding, which may partly reflect differences in substrate location, warrants prospective evaluation.

title: Electrocardiographic imaging of ventricular activation and repolarization in PLN- and PKP2-cardiomyopathy.
summary:
BACKGROUND: 12-lead electrocardiograms, though commonly used in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy diagnosis, lack spatial detail. Electrocardiographic imaging (ECGI) offers a comprehensive assessment of cardiac electrical activity and may better detect electrical abnormalities to identify individuals at risk of disease expression.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize activation and repolarization in Plakophilin-2 (PKP2) and Phospholamban (PLN) pathogenic variant carriers compared to controls.

METHODS: ECGI was used to estimate cardiac activation and repolarization in controls and PKP2-/PLN-carriers. Patterns most frequently observed in controls subjects were classified as normal activation/repolarization; distinct patterns as delayed right/left ventricular (RV/LV) activation/repolarization.

RESULTS: 131 subjects (40 [27;54] years, 55% female) were included: 20 controls and 111 variant carriers with absent or variable phenotypes (54 PKP2, 57 PLN). Ventricular arrhythmias occurred more frequently in PKP2-carriers with delayed RV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (85% vs 21%, P<0.001), and more often in PLN-carriers with delayed LV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (38% vs 0%, P=0.003). T-wave inversions (TWI) in V1-V3 were more often observed in PKP2-carriers with delayed RV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (77% vs 0%, P<0.001), and TWI in V4-V6 were more common in PLN-carriers with delayed LV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (50% vs 4%, P=0.001). Delayed repolarization was also identified in 31% of pre-symptomatic PLN-carriers. Delayed activation was not associated with a more severe phenotype.

CONCLUSION: Delayed repolarization was associated with more severe phenotypic disease expression. As delayed RV/LV repolarization was also identified in a subset of pre-symptomatic variant carriers, ECGI may aid early risk stratification of pathogenic variant carriers.

title: Downregulation of PRDX3 promotes the progression of bradyarrhythmia via inducing ferroptosis and inflammatory macrophage infiltration in cardiac ganglion plexus.
summary:
AIM: Bradyarrhythmia is a prevalent cardiac disorder often necessitating lifelong pacemaker implantation, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study investigated the role of Peroxiredoxin 3 (PRDX3), a mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme, in the pathogenesis of bradyarrhythmia.

METHODS: A rat model of bradyarrhythmia was constructed. In vivo telemetric ECG recording, transcriptome RNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, western blot, reverse transcription-quantitative PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) assay were performed to evaluate the potential function of PRDX3 in bradyarrhythmia.

RESULTS: We observed a significant downregulation of PRDX3 in the cardiac ganglion plexus (CGP) in bradyarrhythmia rats. PRDX3 knockdown in primary CGP cells exhibited hallmark features of ferroptosis, including iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, PRDX3 deficiency led to excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which inactivated the glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) signaling pathway, thereby driving ferroptotic cell death. Restoration of PRDX3 expression in vivo significantly ameliorated bradyarrhythmia, and suppressed inflammatory cytokines production and M1 macrophage infiltration within the sinoatrial node. Furthermore, PRDX3 restoration alleviated ferroptosis and improved cardiac function by stabilizing heart rates and reducing R-R interval variability.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that PRDX3 downregulation promotes bradyarrhythmia progression via inducing ferroptosis and inflammatory M1 macrophage infiltration, revealing a novel role of PRDX3 in bradyarrhythmia.

title: [Outpatient implantation and replacement of pacemakers and implantable defibrillators in German hospitals (2018-2024)].
summary:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Several health policy measures have been implemented in Germany to promote ambulatory care. Outpatient operations and other procedures to replace inpatient stays in hospitals are regulated by § 115b SGB V and in particular the AOP (Ambulante Operationen im Krankenhaus) catalog. The AOP catalog was substantially changed and expanded in 2023. This expansion included additional outpatient procedures regarding implantation and replacement of pacemakers (PM) and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs). Although information on the number of these procedures is available on the level of the individual hospital, aggregated Germany-wide data and analyses is currently lacking. The aim of the current investigation was to analyze the percentage of ambulatory PM and ICD implantations and replacements performed as well as the percentage of hospitals carrying out these procedures in the ambulatory setting during 2018-2024.

METHODS: This secondary data analysis is based on the annual hospital quality reports, which are aggregated in the proprietary BinDoc database. This database was queried using prespecified OPS (operation and procedure key) codes to identify ambulatory and inpatient PM and ICD implantation and replacement procedure numbers. A hospital level analysis was carried out, categorizing whether hospitals performed inpatient only, inpatient + outpatient, or only outpatient procedures.

RESULTS: The percentage of ambulatory PM procedures increased slightly from 2018 (4.3%) to 2022 (8.5%), followed by a steep increase to 12.9% in 2023 and 14.9% in 2024. This trend was apparent for both PM implantations and replacements, for all device types. The percentage of ambulatory PM replacements was higher for all years in the period 2018-2024 with a maximum in year 2024 (replacements: 46.0% [2-chamber PM], 43.2% [1-chamber PM], 36.3% [CRT-P] versus implantation: 7.5% [1-chamber PM], 5.9% [2-chamber PM]). The percentage of ambulatory ICD replacements increased in 2023 and 2024 for all ICD device types with a maximum in 2024 (1-chamber ICD: 40.5%, 2‑chamber ICD: 39.0%, CRT-D: 31.9%). The hospital level analysis showed a strong increase in the percentage of hospitals performing ambulatory PM and ICD procedures in 2023 and 2024.

CONCLUSION: The results suggest that the substantial changes and expansion of the AOP catalog in 2023 have significantly promoted the outpatient implantation and replacement of PM and ICDs in German hospitals. In addition, the results are relevant in light of future development and optimization of outpatient care in Germany.

title: Association Between Hospital Performance and Care Delivery for out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
summary: IntroductionOut-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a leading cause of death worldwide, with substantial variation in survival between hospitals. Differences in post-arrest hospital care may explain this variation. We used a US national claims database to evaluate the association between increasing hospital performance and provision of care interventions.MethodsWe retrospectively studied the 2020-2022 National Emergency Department Sample database. OHCAs were defined by emergency department visits with: (1) an ICD-10 cardiac arrest diagnosis; or, (2) procedure codes for cardiopulmonary resuscitation. We included adult (age >18) patients with an associated hospitalization, excluding ED visits with a disposition of death. The main outcome was provision of hospital care interventions. Hospital performance quartiles were primarily defined by each hospital's proportion of OHCA patients surviving to hospital discharge. Using ordinal logistic regression, we evaluated the association between increasing hospital performance quartile and care intervention, accounting for patient demographics and year of cardiac arrest.ResultsAmong 192,207 patients treated at 1565 hospitals, survival to discharge was higher at top-quartile hospitals than bottom-quartile hospitals (46.0% vs 24.4%). Interventional cardiac procedures were associated with increasing hospital performance (left heart catheterization-aOR 2.0[1.8-2.1]; percutaneous coronary intervention-aOR 1.9[1.8-2.0]; ventricular assist device-aOR 1.8[1.7-2.0]; automatic implantable cardioverter defibrillator-aOR 2.2[2.1-2.4]; extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-aOR 3.3[2.4-4.5]; coronary artery bypass graft-aOR 2.4[2.1-2.7]). Arterial line placement (aOR 1.2[1.04-1.4]) and therapeutic hypothermia (aOR 1.5[1.1-2.3]) were also associated with increasing hospital performance quartile. Other interventions were not associated or were inversely associated with hospital performance: echocardiography, body imaging, head imaging, electroencephalogram, central lines, do not resuscitate orders.ConclusionInterventional cardiac procedures were consistently associated with increasing hospital performance quartile; arterial line placement and therapeutic hypothermia were associated only in our primary analysis. Diagnostic and neuroprognostication procedures were not associated with, or were inversely associated with, increasing hospital performance.

title: Effects of Remote Monitoring of Tachy-Devices: A Systematic Review and Component Network Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Remote monitoring (RM) is a multicomponent intervention that includes scheduled interrogation and automated alerts in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) or cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillators (CRT-Ds); however, the prognostic contribution of its individual components remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the effects of RM components on the prognosis of patients with ICDs or CRT-Ds.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and major clinical trial registries. Randomized controlled trials assessing RM in patients with ICDs or CRT-Ds were included. The primary outcome was hospitalization due to cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or device-related complications. The secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and unscheduled outpatient visits. The risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Data were synthesized using random-effects pairwise meta-analysis, random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA), and additive component NMA (CNMA).

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies with 11,502 patients were included. Pairwise meta-analysis showed that RM-based follow-up reduced heart failure hospitalizations compared to in-person follow-up (risk ratio [RR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.74-0.98). NMA indicated that a configuration combining scheduled remote interrogations (≥1 month), automated alerts, and in-person visits (<12 months) was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality than in-person visits (<12 months) (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.21-0.86). CNMA found no consistent independent associations between the RM components and outcomes.

CONCLUSION: RM reduced heart failure hospitalization, but no individual component showed consistent effects, suggesting that outcomes may depend on the overall configuration rather than isolated components.

title: Pacemaker near 0.1 Hz: A functional framework co-ordinating neural, cardiovascular and visceral systems.
summary: Oscillations near 0.1 Hz are associated with co-ordinated brain-body dynamics across neural, autonomic, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and peripheral systems. Although once dismissed as noise, these slow fluctuations are now recognized as key mediators of resonance across distributed functional axes, including brain-heart and brain-gut interactions. Here, we review multidisciplinary evidence demonstrating that 0.1 Hz oscillations emerge from hierarchical interactions among central pacemakers, baroreceptor feedback, vascular vasomotion and intrinsic organ oscillators. To illustrate, slow breathing at this frequency consistently enhances vagal activity, increases heart rate variability, stabilizes blood pressure and entrains brain and cerebrospinal fluid rhythms, linking autonomic regulation to cognitive and emotional processes. Collectively, we argue that 0.1 Hz represents a systems-level organizing frequency underlying dynamic integration of brain-body physiological and psychological (e.g. emotional, cognitive) processes. Understanding the role of these oscillations offers promising avenues for biofeedback, neuromodulation and clinical interventions especially aimed at improving neuroautonomic and psychophysiological functions.

title: Dual regulation of intracellular Ca2+ oscillations by cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP in colonic interstitial cells of Cajal.
summary: Intracellular Ca²+ ([Ca²+]i) oscillations are involved in the generation of pacemaker potentials in interstitial cells of Cajal (ICC). Cyclic nucleotides, cyclic AMP (cAMP) and cyclic GMP (cGMP), function as key second messengers in diverse cellular signaling pathways; however, their roles in regulating [Ca²+]i oscillations in colonic ICC remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of cAMP and cGMP on [Ca²+]i oscillations associated with pacemaker activity in cultured mouse colonic ICC. Cultured mouse colonic ICC were studied using confocal Ca²+ imaging with fluo-4/AM. Pharmacological modulators of adenylate cyclase, guanylate cyclase, phosphodiesterase, protein kinases, hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels, and nitric oxide signaling were applied to evaluate their effects on spontaneous [Ca²+]i oscillations. Colonic ICC exhibited regular spontaneous [Ca²+]i oscillations from the endoplasmic reticulum. Elevation of intracellular cAMP levels using membrane-permeable cAMP or phosphodiesterase inhibition significantly enhanced [Ca²+]i oscillations, whereas adenylate cyclase inhibition suppressed oscillatory activity. In contrast, elevation of cGMP levels reduced [Ca²+]i oscillations, while guanylate cyclase inhibition enhanced them. Inhibition of protein kinase A or protein kinase G did not significantly affect [Ca²+] i oscillations. Blockade of HCN channels markedly suppressed oscillatory activity, mimicking the effects of adenylate cyclase inhibition. Additionally, inhibition of nitric oxide synthesis enhanced [Ca²+]i oscillations, whereas nitric oxide donation reduced them. Basal pacemaker-associated [Ca²+]i oscillations in colonic ICC are regulated by a dynamic balance between cAMP-dependent facilitation and cGMP-dependent inhibition. Modulation of cyclic nucleotide signaling may provide a physiological basis for therapeutic strategies targeting colonic motility disorders.

title: Clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic features of childhood cardiomyopathy in the United Arab Emirates
summary: BACKGROUND Cardiomyopathy (CMP) is one of the main causes of heart failure in children. Genetic and metabolic etiology are common in regions with high consanguinity. AIM To describe the clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic features of childhood CMP in the United Arab Emirates. METHODS This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in the United Arab Emirates, covering a period from 2020 to 2025. Historical data back to January 2013 were retrieved for survival analysis. All children with CMP were included. Demographic, clinical, electrocardiography, and echocardiography (echo) data were collected. Metabolic and genetic studies were included. RESULTS The study included 200 cases of CMP (60% were female). The cohort comprised 25 ethnic groups, with consanguinity status known for 70 families and positive in 31%. The most common age of presentation was 0-6 months. Syndromic features and neurodevelopmental delays were found in 28% and 33% of the cases, respectively. Long QT syndrome was diagnosed in 9% of the patients. Metabolic screening was positive in 15% of the cohort. The most common abnormalities were conditions associated with high lactate levels (31%), followed by conditions associated with high ammonia levels (15%). Genetic testing was positive in 21.5% of the cohort. The most common genetic abnormality was Noonan’s syndrome, followed by Alström and CHARGE syndromes; the latter, to our knowledge, has not been previously reported. Hypertrophic CMP (HCM) was the most common type (47%), followed by dilated CMP (36.5%), noncompaction CMP (14%), and restrictive CMP (2.5%). Patients with HCM presented significantly earlier and had more associated syndromic features (P < 0.041). There was statistically higher mortality in patients with noncompaction CMP associated with low EF or with HCM (combined) and a higher recovery rate in those with DCM (P < 0.05). The whole cohort mortality rate was 12%, and it was 25% for those with positive genetic testing. The mean (95%CI) of overall survival was 73.8 months. There were significantly lower survival rates in patients with edema. CONCLUSION In this highly consanguineous population, CMP is more prevalent in females and presents mostly in early infancy. The most common type is HCM. Genetic and metabolic disorders are common and are associated with higher mortality rates.

title: Atrial Fibrillation and Aging: The Role of MicroRNA Networks Across Cellular, Structural, and Electrophysiological Remodeling.
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) becomes more common with advancing age, but chronological age does not identify the molecular processes responsible for atrial vulnerability. Human studies document age-associated changes in atrial conduction and microRNA (miRNA) expression, while experimental studies establish miRNA regulation of selected ion channels, fibroblast responses, and intercellular communication. These findings frequently arise from different populations, anatomical regions, and disease models. This narrative review examines how miRNA modules intersect with cellular, structural, and electrophysiological remodeling and defines the evidence required to connect these observations. We frame networked atrial aging as a literature-based conceptual model in which heterogeneous cellular states can influence overlapping atrial phenotypes. Associations, direct target regulation, functional perturbation, and intervention effects are evaluated separately from evidence that aging initiates a pathway. The principal unresolved link is the integration of age-associated miRNA changes with target regulation and altered AF susceptibility within the same biological context. Circulating miRNAs introduce an additional problem because systemic aging and extracardiac sources can influence their abundance independently of atrial mechanisms. Experimental reversibility supports further investigation, but does not establish clinical efficacy. Progress requires anatomically and cell-resolved studies that account for sex, comorbidity, AF-induced remodeling, and the distinction between cellular phenotypes and clinical arrhythmia.

title: Desmoplakin Deficiency Disrupts Mechanotransduction and Calcium Homeostasis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disorder characterized by progressive myocardial dysfunction and life-threatening arrhythmias. Pathogenic variants in DSP, encoding the desmosomal protein desmoplakin, are among the leading causes of ACM. Although desmosomal disruption is central to disease initiation, the mechanisms linking DSP (desmoplakin) deficiency to arrhythmogenesis and adverse cardiac remodeling remain poorly defined. We investigated the molecular basis of DSP deficiency-mediated ACM and evaluated mechanism-based therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: DSP-deficient mice and human iPSC-based engineered heart tissues were established to evaluate arrhythmogenic phenotypes. YAP1 (yes-associated protein 1)-overexpression and Myo5a (myosin Va) depletion models were generated in vivo and in vitro to validate potential mechanistic links between DSP deficiency and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species scavenger MitoTEMPO, adeno-associated virus-mediated CaMKII inhibition using AIP, and genetic introduction of the ryanodine receptor 2-S2814A variant were used to verify mechanism-based therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and CaMKII-dependent calcium dysregulation.

RESULTS: DSP deficiency in vivo and in vitro leads to cytoskeletal disorganization, impaired YAP1-TEAD1 transcriptional activity, and suppressed expression of the mitochondria-skeleton tethering protein Myo5a. These structural and transcriptional alterations are accompanied by mitochondrial impairment, reduced contractile force, and calcium-handling abnormalities in cardiomyocytes. At the tissue and organ levels, these cellular defects increase signal-transduction heterogeneity, ultimately resulting in ventricular arrhythmias. Phenotypic rescue was achieved through multiple interventions: restoring YAP1 signaling, scavenging mitochondrial reactive oxygen species with MitoTEMPO, AAV-mediated CaMKII inhibition with AIP, and genetic introduction of the ryanodine receptor 2-S2814A variant in DSP-deficient iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. All these approaches successfully improved mitochondrial function, restored contractile capability, and alleviated arrhythmia phenotypes in cells, engineered tissues, and mice.

CONCLUSIONS: DSP deficiency drives ACM through a novel mechanotransduction-mitochondrial-calcium signaling axis. These findings elucidate the functional network linking myocardial structure, mitochondrial-calcium homeostasis, and arrhythmic phenotypes, providing potential therapeutic targets for ACM.

title: Sequential Disease-Modifying Therapy and Early Experience with Eplontersen in Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis (p.Thr80Ala) with a Mixed Phenotype: A Case Report.
summary: Background: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) is a progressive multisystem disease, and some patients continue to deteriorate despite disease-modifying therapy. Real-world data on sequential treatment and on eplontersen after prior gene-silencing therapy are scarce. Case Presentation: A 60-year-old man with a family history suggestive of amyloidosis presented in early 2017 with heart failure (NYHA class II-III), chronic diarrhoea and carpal tunnel syndrome. Multimodality imaging, grade 3 bone scintigraphy, exclusion of a monoclonal protein (negative immunofixation and a normal serum free light chain ratio) and genetic testing established ATTRv amyloidosis due to the p.Thr80Ala variant, and colonic and duodenal biopsies showed gastrointestinal amyloid deposits. Between 2017 and 2025 he was treated sequentially with tafamidis, patisiran and vutrisiran. Over this period the disease progressed clinically, with weight loss, worsening axonal polyneuropathy on nerve conduction studies, rising NT-proBNP (up to 3808 pg/mL) and a decline in six-minute walk distance. In July 2025, vutrisiran was replaced by eplontersen. During 15 months of follow-up, eplontersen was well tolerated and body weight increased from 54 to 57 kg. NT-proBNP fluctuated without a sustained further rise (3093 pg/mL at the switch and 3141 pg/mL at 15 months), and troponin T and renal function were unchanged, whereas diarrhoea persisted and the six-minute walk distance was 360 m. Conclusions: This case shows clinical progression of p.Thr80Ala ATTRv amyloidosis despite sequential stabiliser and small interfering RNA therapy, followed by clinical stabilisation after a switch to eplontersen. Without serum TTR measurements and in a single patient, these observations do not allow conclusions about treatment efficacy.

title: Acute Myocarditis: Contemporary Diagnosis, Risk Stratification and Management, with a Focus on Heart Failure and Fulminant Presentations.
summary: Acute myocarditis encompasses a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from mild chest pain with preserved ventricular function to fulminant heart failure, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock and sudden cardiac death. Recent advances have shifted its definition from a primarily histopathological entity toward an integrated clinical syndrome in which multimodality imaging, biomarkers and endomyocardial biopsy contribute to diagnosis and risk assessment. Cardiac magnetic resonance has become central to non-invasive tissue characterization while endomyocardial biopsy remains a relevant approach in high-risk or treatment-refractory patients, allowing identification of histological subtypes that may require specific therapy. Management is largely determined by clinical severity and aetiology, ranging from supportive care and guideline-directed heart failure therapy to immunosuppression, targeted antimicrobial treatment and temporary mechanical circulatory support in fulminant cases. Increasing evidence also highlights the relationship between myocarditis-like episodes and inherited cardiomyopathies, particularly desmosomal disease, in which recurrent "hot phases" may represent an early manifestation of a genetic substrate. Based on a structured literature search, this narrative review summarizes current concepts in the classification, diagnosis, complications and management of acute myocarditis with particular emphasis on heart failure and fulminant presentations, risk stratification and genetic susceptibility. Throughout the text, established treatments are kept separate from emerging mechanism-based strategies, which are still supported by limited evidence.

title: Changes in Community Pharmacists' Self-Assessed Explanatory Ability and Preventive Awareness Following an Integrated Atrial Fibrillation Screening and Community Education Programme: A Longitudinal Study.
summary: This uncontrolled longitudinal study examined changes in community pharmacists' self-assessed explanatory ability and preventive awareness during an integrated e-learning, atrial fibrillation (AF) screening and community education programme. Twenty-seven pharmacists completed five five-point items at baseline (T0), after e-learning (T1) and after practical activities (T2). Friedman tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were supplemented by exact conditional sign-permutation analyses, with Bonferroni correction within each item. Resident health check-up recommendations were assessed using paired counts and a pharmacy-clustered sensitivity analysis. Prevention awareness increased from T0 to T1 (exact p = 0.001953), whereas self-assessed stroke and AF explanation increased from T1 to T2 (p = 0.004395 and 0.004883). Exact comparisons supported T0-T2 increases in self-assessed ability to explain stroke and AF and awareness of prevention; the increase in perceived activity value did not meet the corrected threshold (p = 0.0195). Among 223 repeat participants, recommendations increased from 7.6% to 22.4%, a difference of 14.8 percentage points (pharmacy-clustered 95% CI -4.7 to 34.3). Of 44 free-text responses, 26 were obtained at T0, 10 at T1 and eight at T2. Participation was associated with changes in three self-assessed outcomes. Resident recommendations varied substantially between pharmacies. Although causal effects and clinical benefit remain unestablished, the findings support further evaluation of integrated learning and practice to strengthen pharmacists' contribution to cardiovascular prevention.

title: Development of a Pharmacogenomic-Clinical Model for Acenocoumarol Dose Prediction in Older Vietnamese Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Acenocoumarol maintenance dose varies with clinical and pharmacogenetic factors, but evidence in older Southeast Asian patients is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate a pharmacogenomic-clinical model predicting stable weekly acenocoumarol dose in older Vietnamese patients with atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: We studied 161 patients aged ≥60 years receiving stable acenocoumarol therapy. Clinical factors, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), CYP2C9*3 and VKORC1 -1639G>A were assessed. A clinical model (age and CCI) was compared with an integrated model adding VKORC1. Apparent R2 , mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) were optimism-corrected using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Calibration, residual diagnostics and HC3 robust inference were assessed.

RESULTS: Mean age was 75.64 ± 7.74 years; 56.52% were women. The VKORC1 A-allele frequency was 82.61%, and CYP2C9*3 frequency was 1.55%. Median stable doses were 5.0, 7.0 and 14.0 mg/week in AA, GA and GG carriers, respectively (P<0.001). The integrated model improved apparent R2 from 0.180 to 0.788; optimism-corrected R2 was 0.158 versus 0.783. Optimism-corrected MAE was 1.187 versus 0.698 mg/week and RMSE was 1.667 versus 0.849 mg/week. Heteroscedasticity was detected (Breusch-Pagan P=0.005), and HC3 inference retained significant associations for age, CCI and VKORC1. Excluding three GG carriers reduced adjusted R2 to 0.638.

CONCLUSION: Incorporating VKORC1 improved the internally assessed performance of an exploratory model for estimating stable acenocoumarol maintenance dose. However, the high explained variance was partly influenced by three GG carriers, all receiving 14.0 mg/week; this small subgroup limits the precision and generalizability of genotype-specific predictions. Independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.
